title: What's Inside a Dead EV Battery? The Numbers ♻️🔋 #shorts

scenes.text: When an E V battery dies, is it trash? Let's run the numbers.
A big five-hundred-kilo pack holds roughly fifty kilos of nickel, thirty of copper, and ten each of cobalt and lithium.
Recyclers shred the old cells, then use chemistry to dissolve and purify the metals back out.
Redwood Materials says it recovers more than ninety-five percent of the lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper.
A Stanford study of its plant found recycled metals cut emissions fifty-eight to eighty-one percent versus mining, with far less water and energy.
Metals don't wear out, so they can go back into new batteries again and again.
So could the biggest lithium mine of the future be a pile of old batteries? Follow EV Drive.
